answer: Each agent maintains a cryptographic vault of reputation tokens earned by solving verifiable tasks posted in a distributed canyon of challenge contracts. When a new identity registers, it must deposit a stake into the harbor pool and answer a randomly selected honeypot query whose correct reply is known only to honest validators; a wrong answer burns the stake and flags the identity. An attacker therefore pays per fake node both the full deposit and the computational cost of solving the hidden puzzles, making a large‑scale Sybil attack economically prohibitive.
